page_title: Text skew correction with OpenCV and Python - PyImageSearch

summary.title: Text skew correction with OpenCV and Python
summary.one_liner: You learn to deskew a rotated block of text in an image by thresholding it, computing a minimum-area rotated bounding box with cv2.minAreaRect, and applying an affine rotation with OpenCV.
takeaways: Invert and binarize the image with Otsu thresholding so text pixels are foreground.
Use cv2.minAreaRect on the foreground pixel coordinates to get the skew angle, adjusting for its [-90, 0) range.
Rotate the image with cv2.getRotationMatrix2D and cv2.warpAffine to correct the skew.
The method was tested on four images rotated between 4 and 41 degrees in both directions.
summary.summary: This PyImageSearch tutorial is a Python and OpenCV implementation of Félix Abecassis's text skew correction approach. The script converts an image to grayscale, inverts it, and applies Otsu thresholding, then computes a minimum rotated bounding box around the text pixels to estimate the angle. It then rotates the image with an affine transformation to deskew it. The author evaluates the code on a small dataset of four text images rotated between 4 and 41 degrees, clockwise and counter-clockwise, and notes its use in document digitization pipelines before OCR.
